label: Partial trial 1 — 5 entries across Layers 2, 5, 6

scope.note: Trial: EU AI Act, China AI Law (missing link), US Frontier AI Access EO (secondary-only link), EU GPAI Code (voluntary), Anthropic RSP (corporate). Discovery: EU, and Anthropic (Layer 6).

discovery.area: EU (jurisdiction, B1) — new mechanisms and institutions since June 2026
discovery.summary: I ran web searches for EU AI Act amendments, new codes of practice, guidelines and AI Office mechanisms. The search tool worked, but every candidate's primary source (digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu, eur-lex.europa.eu) and every secondary page was blocked. So these are leads only: nothing here is verified, and nothing is proposed.
queries: EU AI Act digital omnibus delay high-risk obligations 2026
European Commission AI Act new guidelines code of practice August September 2026
GPAI Code of Practice signatories update 2026 AI Office

candidates.name: Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
candidates.result: lead — update to existing entry (eu-aia); source inaccessible
candidates.reason: An amending regulation. Reported in force 27 Jul 2026, moving the high-risk dates. Would change eu-aia (desc, timing), and probably eu-aio and the gap and FAQ text that mention Aug 2026/2027. Probably not a separate entry.

candidates.name: Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content (Art. 50)
candidates.result: lead — possible new entry (L5, eu); source inaccessible
candidates.reason: A voluntary code linked to the Article 50 transparency duties for generative AI providers. Would qualify under RUBRIC §1 if adopted. Secondary sources disagree on the dates (draft 5 Mar or 8 May 2026; final 10 Jun 2026?).

candidates.name: Commission guidelines on Article 50 (draft, May 2026)
candidates.result: lead — context for the code above
candidates.reason: Interpretive guidance rather than a separate mechanism; would be noted in the code's or eu-aia's context.

candidates.name: AI Office GPAI Code 'Signatory Taskforce' (first met 30 Jan 2026)
candidates.result: screened out as a separate entry; lead for gpai-cop context
candidates.reason: An implementation forum of an existing mechanism.

candidates.name: GPAI enforcement powers applying from 2 Aug 2026
candidates.result: lead — update to existing entries (eu-aia, eu-aio)
candidates.reason: A date that has passed since the snapshot. The map's FAQ says the AI Office's 'full enforcement powers activate in August 2026'. That wording may need a tense change once verified.

discovery.limits: No primary source was opened, so absence of other candidates means nothing. This search must be repeated once network access is fixed.

discovery.area: Anthropic (lab, B4) — new governance documents and mechanisms
discovery.summary: I read the RSP page, the v3 announcement, the Frontier Safety Roadmap and the Transparency Hub on anthropic.com. The policy PDF (www-cdn.anthropic.com), the HTML policy text and the Trust Center were blocked.

candidates.name: Frontier Safety Roadmap (Feb 2026)
candidates.result: screened out as a separate entry; part of rsp
candidates.reason: Created by RSP v3 and described as 'public goals', not commitments. It belongs in the rsp entry, not in a new one. Folded into P-0010's follow-up.

candidates.name: Risk Reports (Feb and Aug 2026)
candidates.reason: Implementation evidence under RSP v3; recorded in P-0007.

candidates.name: RSP Noncompliance Reporting and Anti-Retaliation Policy (updated Mar 2026)
candidates.result: screened out — minor; note for baseline
candidates.reason: An internal compliance policy tied to the RSP. It could be added to the rsp accountability note later. Not material enough for a separate entry.

candidates.name: Frontier Compliance Framework
candidates.reason: Anthropic's compliance document for SB 53, RAISE and the EU Code. Evidence of the relationship, not a separate mechanism; it supports the new RAISE↔RSP connection.

candidates.name: Transparency Hub
candidates.reason: A publication channel (model reports), not a governance mechanism. Useful as implementation evidence.

discovery.limits: The policy text itself was not read. Other labs were not searched; that is outside this trial.

usage: Not measured per run. The platform's session total was $12.34 (input 90k, output 182k, cache-read 17.6M tokens) as of 9 Oct; that covers all workflow design, tooling and research in this session since 8 Oct, not this run alone.
highlights: **Source access is still the blocker.** The environment's network policy blocks every EU, US federal, US state, UK and Chinese government site and the RSP v3.4 PDF; only www.anthropic.com loads. Nothing that depends on those sources is verified, and those proposals sit in §B.
**Verified externally:** the RSP version history (v3.4, 8 Jul 2026; eight revisions since v1.0), its 2026 accountability additions, and that RSP v1.0 (Sep 2023) predates the Seoul commitments.

**Internal consistency only:** the data.json count, the FAQ list of binding laws, the 'Asia (other)' label, the Layer 2 subtitle and the date wording. These check the map against itself, not against the world.

**Held as a group:** the RSP version update (P-0005) is not applied with only the version changed, because the retained ASL and threshold wording is unverified. Its two companion edits wait with it so the entry stays coherent.

**Revised after your review:** P-0002 narrowed to internal consistency (v2, needs your decision); P-0009 reattributed to Anthropic and held for source access (v2); P-0003's approval clarified as covering only the label (other-aisis is now P-0011).
